title: Nowhere dense images through a finite closed section cover
statement: Let $q:W\to X$ be a finite locally free morphism of schemes [def-pc-finite-locally-free]. Suppose there are finitely many closed subschemes $i_j:W_j\hookrightarrow W$ [def-weil-closed-immersion] whose underlying sets cover $|W|$, and each composite $W_j\to W\to X$ is an isomorphism. If $A\subseteq|W|$ is closed and nowhere dense (the interior of its closure is empty), then $q(A)$ is closed and nowhere dense in $|X|$.

source.place: Tag 03HX, proof after Tag 03HW: the paragraph beginning 'Assume that Y is a finite union of closed subsets' and the contradiction paragraph.

proof.text: Write $C_j=i_j(|W_j|)\subseteq|W|$. By [def-weil-closed-immersion], $C_j$ is closed and $|W_j|\to C_j$ is a homeomorphism. The isomorphism $q i_j$ and its inverse induce inverse continuous maps, so $h_j=q|_{C_j}:C_j\to|X|$ is a homeomorphism. Put $B_j=A\cap C_j$ and $E_j=h_j(B_j)$. Each $B_j$ is closed in $C_j$, hence each $E_j$ is closed in $|X|$. The cover gives $q(A)=\bigcup_j E_j$, a finite union of closed subsets, so $q(A)$ is closed. If the index set is empty then $W$ and $A$ are empty and the conclusion holds.

source.place: Tag 03HX, lemma-image-nowhere-dense-finite, finite closed section-cover paragraph and its contradiction argument

proof.text: Fix a section, relabelled $C_1$. Suppose $B_1$ contains a nonempty relatively open subset $V\subseteq C_1$. Process the remaining finitely many $C_j$ one at a time, maintaining that $V$ is nonempty, open in $C_1$, contained in $B_1$, and for every processed index either $V\subseteq C_j$ or $V\cap C_j=\varnothing$. Since $C_j$ is closed [def-weil-closed-immersion], $V\cap C_j$ is closed in $V$. If it is a proper subset, replace $V$ by its nonempty open complement $V\setminus C_j$. Otherwise retain $V$. Shrinking preserves all earlier decisions and the maintained properties. This gives a partition $I_1\amalg I_2$ of the indices with $1\in I_1$, $V\subseteq C_j$ for $j\in I_1$ and $V\cap C_j=\varnothing$ for $j\in I_2$.

source.place: Tag 03HX, lemma-image-nowhere-dense-finite, finite closed section-cover paragraph and its contradiction argument

proof.text: Set $U=h_1(V)$, a nonempty open subset of $|X|$. For $j\in I_1$, the inclusion $V\subseteq C_j$ and injectivity of $h_j$ show $C_j\cap q^{-1}(U)=V$: a point over $x\in U$ must be the unique point of $V$ over $x$. For $j\in I_2$, $C_j$ misses $V$. Using the cover of $|W|$ therefore gives $V=q^{-1}(U)\setminus\bigcup_{j\in I_2}C_j$. This is open in $|W|$: $q$ is continuous and the union on the right is a finite union of closed subsets [def-weil-closed-immersion]. But $\varnothing\ne V\subseteq A$, contradicting that the closed subset $A$ has empty interior. Thus every $B_j$ has empty interior in $C_j$.

source.place: Tag 03HX, lemma-image-nowhere-dense-finite, finite closed section-cover paragraph and its contradiction argument

proof.text: For each $j$, a nonempty open subset of $|X|$ contained in $E_j$ would have nonempty open inverse image under $h_j$ contained in $B_j$, contrary to the preceding steps. Thus the closed subsets $E_j$ all have empty interior. To finish, the union of two closed subsets $D,F$ of empty interior also has empty interior: if $O\subseteq D\cup F$ is open, then $O\setminus F$ is open and contained in $D$, hence empty; consequently $O\subseteq F$, hence $O=\varnothing$. Induction on the finite index set, starting with the empty subset, shows $q(A)=\bigcup_j E_j$ has empty interior. Since it is closed by step 1, it is nowhere dense. This is the elementary finite-union argument in Topology Tag 03HO (lemma-nowhere-dense), written out here rather than made a new node.
